system:
You are evaluating draft replies from an automated customer-support agent for Spotify's Twitter support account, as it operated in 2017.

Score the CANDIDATE REPLY on five criteria, each an integer 1-5.

correctness - Is what it says actually true for Spotify, and does it address what the customer asked?
  1 = wrong or answers a different question   3 = partially right, or vague but not wrong
  5 = accurate and on-point

groundedness - Is every claim supported by the PRECEDENTS shown?
  1 = main claims appear nowhere in the precedents   3 = loosely related to them
  5 = every factual claim traceable to a precedent

consistency - Does it handle this the way the precedents show Spotify handled similar cases (same action, same level of caution, same register)?
  1 = contradicts how Spotify handled these   3 = plausible but diverges
  5 = matches the precedents' approach

helpfulness - Does it move the customer forward?
  1 = useless or pure deflection   3 = generic but usable
  5 = a clear next step or a real answer

no_unsupported_claims - Does it avoid inventing policies, prices, timeframes, or promising account actions (refunds, resets, unlocks) the agent cannot perform?
  1 = makes a promise or states a policy with no support   3 = borderline hedged claim
  5 = makes no unsupported claim at all

Judge only the reply in front of you. The REFERENCE REPLY is what Spotify actually sent; it is context, not a target - a different but equally good reply should score well, and copying the reference does not automatically score 5.

Return ONLY JSON:
{"correctness": n, "groundedness": n, "consistency": n, "helpfulness": n, "no_unsupported_claims": n, "rationale": "<one sentence>"}
prompt:
CUSTOMER MESSAGE:
hi there! My bands music is mixed up with another artists (of the same name) is there a way to change this? :-)

PRECEDENTS:

[2018432] past customer: Do you think you guys can make an update where on the artist page it shows their genre and even on the albums of artists
     spotify replied: Hey there, That sounds like a great idea! Suggest it in our Community at <link> and get support from other users

[1965634] past customer: yo! Is there a way to improve our listed 'related artists'. They're all very different in style to us.
     spotify replied: Hey! We have some info on this here: <link> If you have any questions, just head over to <link> 🙂

[1962023] past customer: needs to fix this problem when two different artist have the same name and it mixes up on both profiles confusing the fans!!
     spotify replied: Hi! Can you send over the URIs of the contents that should be on a separate page? Just right-click the track > Share > URI

[2312956] past customer: Any chance you can seperate new #albumsyoumusthear from new #singles. It's the most annoying thing ever!!
     spotify replied: We can see how that'd be handy. Thanks for taking the time to reach out – your feedback's been noted 📝

[2485950] past customer: the names of the artist and release have been mixed up for years. Is it possible to correct them? <link>
     spotify replied: Hi there! Thanks for reporting. Can you send us over the URI's of the artist's pages and the albums that should be on separate pages? Just right-click the track > Share > URI. We'll take a look backstage 🔍

CANDIDATE REPLY (score this):
Hey there, That sounds like a great idea! Suggest it in our Community at <link> and get support from other users

REFERENCE REPLY actually sent by Spotify (context only):
Hi James! You can contact our Artist team here: <link> If you've already reached out, DM us your email address & we'll chase it up. Let us know

Return the JSON scores.
text: {"correctness":1,"groundedness":5,"consistency":1,"helpfulness":1,"no_unsupported_claims":5,"rationale":"The reply is grounded in a precedent but incorrectly treats an artist-page mix-up as a feature suggestion, failing to request the relevant URIs or direct the artist to the appropriate support team."}
